transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-07-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Patel (Redwood SE), Rajiv Menon (CTO, Nova Labs), Emily Porter (Lead ML Engineer), Carlos Ruiz (Infra)

Summary:
Redwood team ran a migration-focused demo showing API parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood, walked through Console, Optimize recommendations (batching, quantization), and discussed Dedicated vs Hosted and Private/VPC options. Customer raised questions about function calling parity, streaming/parsing differences, token counts, SSO/KMS/ audit logs. Agreed next steps: share parity table, run pilot, schedule benchmark.

Topics Covered:
- API parameter mapping (temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop, presence/ frequency penalties)
- Function/tool calling and structured outputs mapping
- Streaming behaviour and chunking differences
- Embeddings and rate limits, batching recommendations from Redwood Optimize
- Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private trade-offs (latency/cost/data residency)
- Security: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs, data retention
- Benchmark/POC plan and pricing/pilot contract

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're excited to walk through a migration path from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together into Redwood and show the parity mappings and the console. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Rajiv: Good, thanks. We basically want to know how close we can get in terms of API semantics and perf, and what the lift is.
[00:12] Sofia: Totally. I'll hand to Liam for the deep dive on API mapping, and then Aisha will jump into Console and Optimize.
[00:18] Liam: Cool, thanks Sofia. Uh quick agenda: mapping endpoints, model equivalents, streaming & function call behavior, then demo of a small app migrating a chat flow.
[00:30] Emily: Quick thing - we use a combination of OpenAI and Anthropic models, and a few Together variants for internal research, so two asks: 1) identical response formats for our parsers, 2) same safety/temper filtering behavior.
[00:40] Liam: Great, we'll call those out. Starting with model parity: for OpenAI gpt-4 style calls we recommend Redwood model rdx-4-large (example name), for Anthropic claude-like we map to rdx-claude-compat tier, and Together models map to rdx-together-compat. Note: names in the platform are examples, exact model tags will be in the parity doc.
[01:05] Carlos: Are the tokenization differences going to break our logics? We count tokens for pricing.
[01:12] Liam: Good question - tokenization can differ. Redwood exposes the tokenizer model and provides token_count endpoint. We add a small delta note in parity table; also Optimize recommends batching or prefix caching to reduce total tokens.
[01:30] Sofia: A couple product notes: streaming chunks are slightly different - Redwood streams with chunk boundaries at 256B or sentence breaks depending on model; that can change partial response shapes. We have a streaming SDK that normalizes chunking for you.
[01:45] Rajiv: Function calling - we heavily use OpenAI function calling with structured outputs. Is there a 1:1 mapping?
[01:50] Liam: We support function/tool calling and structured outputs, yes. There are a few minor differences: Redwood uses a 'tools' param and returns a tool_call object with name and args, whereas OpenAI returns a function_call field; our SDK ensures compatibility and there's a parity helper that rewrites call shapes. We'll include example code for Node/Python.
[02:20] Emily: Does that affect latency for us? We're latency-sensitive for chat.
[02:25] Aisha: The overhead is negligible, it's mostly JSON shaping in the SDK. Bigger latency factors are model selection (rdx-4-large vs rdx-4-small), batching and KV cache locality. For chat live inference we recommend pinned instances or Dedicated capacity.
[02:45] Carlos: Dedicated - what's the difference vs hosted? We need predictable p95 latency and data isolation.
[02:52] Sofia: Right - Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with isolation and predictable throughput; Hosted is multi-tenant and cheaper but contention can vary (we have SLAs for higher tiers). Private/VPC is an option if you need customer-managed networking and on-prem is possible for air-gapped.
[03:10] Rajiv: Security - do you have SOC2 and KMS details? Need to know about key custody and audit logs.
[03:16] Liam: We are SOC2 Type II compliant, and we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS / HSM integrations) in Private and Dedicated. Audit logs and full request tracing live in the Console; we'll share the security pack.
[03:30] Sofia: Ok I'm gonna share my screen, Liam will run the API parity demo first - you'll see a side-by-side of an OpenAI call and the Redwood equivalent.
[03:38] [Screen share starts]
[03:45] Liam: First example: OpenAI chat completion call, messages array, temperature 0.2, top_p 0.95. On Redwood you'd use /v1/generate with inputs/messages or the chat helper. The mapping in the parity doc shows parameter translation: temperature -> temperature, top_p -> top_p, max_tokens -> max_tokens, stop -> stop. Penalties are mapped similarly but names differ slightly (frequency_penalty -> freq_penalty).
[04:10] Emily: Any gotchas on stop sequences? We rely on multi-token stop sequences in our parser.
[04:16] Liam: Redwood supports multi-token stop sequences; behavior is the same, but when streaming you may see partial tokens - our SDK can buffer until stop detected.
[04:30] Liam: Next - function calling demo. OpenAI call: function_call: {name: 'get_user', arguments: '...'}, Redwood equivalent uses tools param. Demo where the model calls a tool and we invoke it.
[04:50] [Slight audio glitch]
[05:00] Liam: And you can choose to let the platform auto-invoke or return the tool call payload for your app to run. We also have a function call simulator in the Console.
[05:20] Rajiv: Nice. We have parsing logic expecting the OpenAI response JSON shape; will the SDK's rewrite affect us?
[05:26] Aisha: Our migration helper rewrites either side - we can output a OpenAI-shaped object for minimal code changes. For microservices that expect exact shapes we recommend the SDK shim.
[05:40] Carlos: Let's talk about embeddings and reranking - we do heavy embedding work and retrival.
[05:46] Liam: Embeddings map straightforwardly: endpoint differences are documented; we support batch embed and have a recommended batch size per model. Optimize will recommend batch sizes to maximize throughput and reduce token cost. Also we expose cache TTL options.
[06:10] Emily: Rate limits? We saw some rate limits earlier during our tests.
[06:14] Sofia: For Hosted there are soft rate limits tied to plan; Dedicated has explicit throughput. We can do burst capacity. We'll include rate-limit numbers in the parity doc and pilot contract.
[06:30] Liam: Ok switching to Console - Aisha?
[06:34] Aisha: Yeah showing Console now: model catalog, per-model perf profiles, route configuration, and Optimize suggestions. Here you can pin model versions, set rollout policies (canary/A-B), and enable automatic fallback to cheaper variants.
[07:00] [Console screen: Optimize recommendations]
[07:05] Aisha: For your use-case we see recommendations: enable prefix KV caching for chat history > 512 tokens, lower streaming chunk size for mobile clients, and enable 4-bit quantized variant for non-latency-sensitive reranking jobs to save cost.
[07:25] Rajiv: Can Optimize run our historical traces to estimate cost savings?
[07:29] Aisha: Yes, you can upload traces or run a synthetic trace; Optimize runs simulations and gives estimated token and $ savings and a suggested quantization/profile mapping. We'll demo that in the pilot.
[07:45] Emily: We use SAML SSO - any issues with RBAC?
[07:49] Liam: We support SSO/SAML and fine-grained RBAC in Console. For Private deployments we can hook into your IdP directly.
[08:00] Rajiv: About observability - do you provide per-request token breakdown and cost attribution to teams?
[08:06] Aisha: Yes Console shows token-level cost, model latency histograms, traces and logs. You can tag requests and get per-route dashboards.
[08:20] Carlos: Networking - we're strict about egress and VPC peering. How does Private/VPC work?
[08:24] Sofia: Private gives you a control plane with customer-managed networking; we set up a VPC endpoint and you can use AWS PrivateLink or similar. On-prem package is available for air-gapped environments. We'll need your network CIDs and firewall rules.
[08:45] Rajiv: Okay good. Next - concrete migration examples please.
[08:50] Liam: I'll run a mini app: original flow uses OpenAI chat completions plus function calls to enrich entity data, and embeddings for retrieval. I will paste an example request and show Redwood equivalent, then run both and compare tokens and latency.
[09:10] [Liam runs side-by-side calls]
[09:30] Liam: Results: OpenAI response time p95 ~220ms, Redwood hosted equivalent p95 ~240ms on this region - close, within margin. On Dedicated we can get p95 down to ~130ms depending on model size. Token counts were within 2-3% due to tokenizer differences.
[09:55] Emily: Can we get more deterministic latency - p99 spikes are problematic.
[10:00] Aisha: For strict SLOs we recommend Dedicated with pinned instances and pre-warmed KV caches; also set up autoscale policies with reserved capacity. We'll show configuration in the pilot.
[10:20] Carlos: For the pilot, can we vet data residency? We must keep logs within EU region for certain data types.
[10:26] Sofia: Of course - we support region pinning and can restrict logs retention and region for storage. Private deployments give you full control.
[10:40] Rajiv: Pricing - ballpark comparison to OpenAI?
[10:44] Sofia: Hosted pricing is competitive; Dedicated is commit-based (monthly). For heavy workloads Redwood's batching and Optimize typically reduces unit cost by 20-40% in our benchmarks - we'll send a tailored pricing sheet.
[11:00] [15 minute skip summary; discussion continues on edge cases in function calling and streaming]
[26:00] Liam: One edge case: when you stream structured JSON the ephemeral partial chunks can break your JSON parser - we provide a parser helper that buffers until complete JSON. In our tests this solved most issues.
[27:10] Emily: Good. We also need to test safety/filters. Our production path relies on Anthropic safety layers.
[27:20] Liam: Redwood supports model-level safety profiles and content filters. We can apply a safety pre-filter and post-filter. We'll put recommended settings in the security pack.
[28:00] Rajiv: Any notable breaking changes from Together models? We have a few hallucination-prone prompts we tuned.
[28:08] Liam: Model behavior differs; parity is approximate. Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets - we can run your prompt set and show differences, plus recommend quantization and model variants to match behavior.
[29:00] Aisha: Demo of Optimize run: upload prompt set -> run simulated traffic -> get cost/latency/quality deltas -> get model/quantization recommendations. You can then schedule an A/B rollout.
[30:00] Rajiv: For the pilot: what's the data we need to share?
[30:05] Sofia: Sample prompts, representative traffic pattern, network constraints, and any compliance docs. We'll run a 48-hour Dedicated pilot with your traces if you want.
[30:20] Emily: We will provide prompts and a subset of traffic for a benchmark. Also we need to loop in InfoSec.
[30:26] Sofia: We'll share security deck and SOC2, ISO docs. We'll also set up an InfoSec call next week.
[30:40] Carlos: Integration effort - do you provide migration helpers or scripts?
[30:45] Liam: Yes, we have migration SDK shims and example repo that translates OpenAI/Anthropic/Together calls into Redwood's API. We'll share the repo link.
[31:00] [Brief cross talk]
[31:20] Rajiv: One more question: function call cost comparisons - if a lot of our work happens in tools invocation, what's cost delta?
[31:28] Liam: Tools invocations are charged by execution (and tokens). If you migrate to smaller models for the tool execution step, you can save a lot. Optimize's recommendations often suggest tiering model sizes for tool vs. open-ended completion.
[31:50] Aisha: Also consider prefix caching and partial response caching for stable prompts.
[32:10] Emily: Can we see the compare sheet now?
[32:14] Sofia: I'll paste a link in the chat - parity mapping doc, pricing summary, and benchmark template. (link: https://redwood.example.com/parity/nova-labs) - placeholder link.
[32:30] Rajiv: Great. Any blockers for us to start pilot?
[32:34] Sofia: Need NDA/pilot contract, sample prompts, and networking info. We can provision Dedicated test env within 48 hours once contract signed.
[32:50] Carlos: Regarding logging retention, can we set retention to 90 days and sample logs for compliance?
[32:55] Liam: Yes, configurable retention and export to your SIEM. We'll include audit log options in the security docs.
[33:20] [Mid-call housekeeping]
[33:45] Rajiv: Ok let's talk timeline - if we do pilot mid-July, production could be by September depending on results?
[33:52] Sofia: Sounds reasonable. Pilot in mid-July, run 2-4 weeks, then expand to Dedicated by August and production Sept depending on contract.
[34:10] Emily: We'll want to automate the Canary and A-B tests in Console. How programmable is Console?
[34:17] Aisha: Console has an API and Terraform provider for route and rollout configs. You can automate canary policies and automatic fallback.
[34:35] Carlos: For billing/chargeback, can we attribute usage to teams and routes?
[34:38] Aisha: Yes route-level attribution and tags let you bill back to your internal cost centers.
[35:00] [Late call: specifics on benchmarks and test harness]
[40:00] Liam: We're going to run a benchmark: take your sample prompts, run on OpenAI/Anthropic/Together copies then run on Redwood hosted and Dedicated; measure p50/p95/p99, token counts, and quality via your eval prompts. We'll put results in shared sheet.
[41:10] Rajiv: Will you run within our EU region?
[41:15] Sofia: Yes we'll pin region per request; for Private/Dedicated we can provision in EU.
[42:00] Emily: Questions about rate limiting during spike traffic - do you offer graceful degradation?
[42:06] Liam: We have fallback policies: if a model is overloaded we can route to a cheaper compatible variant or degrade to non-streaming to preserve throughput. We can also return cached responses for deterministic queries.
[42:30] Rajiv: That's helpful.
[43:00] [Wrap-up: recap of next steps]
[43:10] Sofia: Recap - action items: Liam to send parity table and migration repo; Sofia to send pricing and pilot contract; Emily to send prompt set; Carlos to provide network constraints. We'll schedule InfoSec call and benchmark run for 2025-07-14.
[43:40] Rajiv: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[43:44] Emily: Thank you.
[43:46] Sofia: Thanks all, we'll follow up in chat with links and docs.
[43:50] [Call ends]

Notes on transcript quality: some small audio glitches and minor transcription errors (function_call vs tool_call naming inconsistent in raw speech).

Attachments/links referenced in call:
- Parity mapping doc (shared live): https://redwood.example.com/parity/nova-labs
